skill.name: git-workflow

skill.summary: Standardizes everyday Git workflow decisions for commits, branches, reviews, and releases.

content.value_statement: Inconsistent Git habits slow reviews, releases, and incident fixes. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code clear workflow rules.
actual_capabilities: Defines Conventional Commits message formats and examples.
Provides branch naming patterns for features, bug fixes, and hotfixes.
Explains GitFlow roles for main, develop, feature, release, and hotfix branches.
Suggests a pre-commit checklist for secrets and quality gates.
Auto-invokes for commit, push, branch, merge, pull request, and release work.
limitations: Does not enforce repository branch protection settings.
Does not create commits or pull requests by itself.
Does not replace project-specific release policies.
Quality gate commands depend on scripts available in the target repository.

use_cases.title: Prepare Clean Commits
use_cases.description: Draft consistent commit messages and confirm staged changes meet basic quality checks.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Feature Branches
use_cases.description: Name branches consistently and align feature work with a shared GitFlow process.

use_cases.title: Review Release Changes
use_cases.description: Use branch and commit conventions to organize release or hotfix work before merging.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Commit Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my staged changes and suggest a Conventional Commits message with a short subject.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Branch Name
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest a branch name for this task using the type, ticket ID, and a concise description.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my current branch and propose a pull request summary, test notes, and review checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Release Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Map these feature, release, and hotfix changes to a GitFlow sequence with merge targets and verification steps.

output_examples.input: Need a commit message for a new OAuth login feature.
output_examples.output: Suggested message: feat(auth): add OAuth2 login support. Include test notes for login success, failed login, and token refresh.

output_examples.input: Need a branch for ticket CORE-456 about null response handling.
output_examples.output: Suggested branch: bugfix/CORE-456-fix-null-response. Use it for the fix, tests, and pull request review.

output_examples.input: Preparing a hotfix for a production security issue.
output_examples.output: Start from main, use a hotfix branch, verify the patch, then merge back to main and develop.

best_practices: Keep commit subjects short, specific, and written in the imperative mood.
Run project quality gates before asking for review.
Use the smallest branch scope that matches the change.
anti_patterns: Mixing unrelated work into one commit or pull request.
Using vague branch names that hide the ticket or intent.
Skipping tests or secret checks before pushing changes.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitFlow?
faq.answer: No. It describes GitFlow patterns, but teams can adapt the guidance to simpler branch models.

faq.question: Can it write commit messages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest Conventional Commits messages based on staged or described changes.

faq.question: Does it run Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and checklist commands for the user or agent to apply.

faq.question: Does it detect secrets?
faq.answer: It suggests a basic staged diff search, but dedicated secret scanning is still recommended.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it suitable for release work?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes branch guidance for releases and hotfixes, including merge targets.
